Gender: Mens [2] 7. Manufacturer parent company: Nidecker Group (NDK Group), acquired Bataleon (via Low Pressure Studio) in 2018 [3] 8. Brand founded: 2000 in the Netherlands by biophysicist Jorgen Karlsen [4] 9. Brand founded (alternate source): 2001 [5] 10. Brand headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Low Pressure Studio) [6] 11. Manufacturing location (current, source A): Austria, at the CAPiTA Mothership factory [7] 12. Manufacturing location (current, source B — DISAGREEMENT): Manufacturing moved from Austria to Asia (Titan factory, China), then possibly Saudi Arabia — multiple conflicting sources on current location [8] 13. Manufacturing location (historic): Originally at Elan factory in Feistritz, Austria; briefly outsourced to Asia; returned to Austria when Capita bought the Mothership [9] 14. Design studio: Low Pressure Studio, Amsterdam [6] 15. Disaster model first available: At least as early as the 2012/2013 season based on evo outlet listings for 2014 model and snowboarding forum posts referencing "2013 Bataleon Disaster" [10] 16. The Disaster has been described as a "long-standing staple in Bataleon's line" as of 2019 [11] 17. Model series: Part of Bataleon's freestyle/park lineup; also available in Women's and Plus (+) variants [12] 18. Related/upgraded model: Disaster+ (Plus Series) — adds carbon stringers, C.S.T. Super Tubes, Aramid X-Ply, lighter core [13] 19. Women's variant: 2027 Bataleon Women's Disaster, flex 2/10 [14] 20. Pro model association: Rixon pro model [2] 21. Available sizes: 151cm, 154cm, 157cm, 153cm Wide, 156cm Wide [2] 22. Shape: True Twin [2] 23. Camber type: Low Camber with 3BT and SideKick, Low Nose Sidebase Uplift and Low Tail Sidebase Uplift [2] 24. Flex rating (merchant): 3/10 [2] 25. Flex rating (S2AS for 2027 Men's Disaster): 2/10 — Soft, ultra-playful [15] — DISAGREEMENT: The merchant lists 3/10 while S2AS lists the 2027 Men's Disaster at 2/10. Bataleon's own site for the prior-year Disaster also lists flex 2. The 3/10 rating may apply to the Disaster+ variant. 26. Flex feel on snow (per SnowboardingProfiles review): Medium-Soft, feels 3/10 on snow despite 2/10 stated rating [16] 27. Flex category (per evo): "Soft" — evo classifies 1-2 ratings as soft, 3-5 as medium [17] 28. Base technology: Triple Base Technology (3BT) — reduces risk of edge-catch while maintaining ollie power and carving control [2] 29. SideKick technology: Amplifies sidebase uplift beyond widest points of nose and tail, giving tips a hull-like shape for enhanced float and smoother turn initiation [2] 30. Nose sidebase uplift: Low [2] 31. Tail sidebase uplift: Low [2] 32. 3BT variant: Jib 3BT — widest centerbase in range, least sidebase uplift [18] 33. Width options: Standard, Wide [2] 34. Mounting pattern: 2x4 Inserts [2] 35. Number of inserts: 24 [19] 36. Insert material: A-grade German stainless steel [20] 37. Laminate: Bi-Ax (bi-axial fibreglass) — lightweight, strong, and playful, responsive yet torsionally forgiving [2] 38. Core: Core Core — full poplar core reinforced with two hardwood beech stringers [2] 39. Core wood species: Poplar with beech hardwood stringers [21] 40. Sidewall: Flex Walls — Urethane poured sidewalls instead of standard ABS [2] 41. Sidewall technology description: Exceptional shock absorption, reducing chatter and vibration for smoother, more stable ride [20] 42. Base: Hyper Glide S — standard sintered base, fast and durable [2] 43. Terrain: Park, Rails, Jumps, Groomers [2] 44. Rider level: Intermediate [2] 45. Price at SkatePro (USD, prior-year Disaster): $429.95 — in stock [22] 80. Price at SnowboardingProfiles reference (USD): $499 [16] 81. Previous-year Disaster sale price at Exodus Ride Shop (CHF): CHF 237 (regular CHF 394) [23] 82. Price at Blauer Board Shop: 2027 model listed but requires login [24] 83. S2AS (Surface 2 Air Sports): 2027 Men's Disaster listed, UK-based authorized retailer with price match [15] 84. Evo: Stocks the Disaster+ variant (2026 model currently); free shipping & lowest price guarantee [25] 85. The-House: Stocks Bataleon Disaster, lists flex 3/10 and 24 inserts [19] 86. Backcountry.com: Stocks Bataleon boards, some with up to 40% discount on prior-year models [26] 87. Warranty: 2-year limited warranty against manufacturing defects from authorized dealer [27] 88. Extended warranty: 2+1 year warranty — register product and sign up for newsletter to get 3rd year [28] 89. Return policy (Bataleon direct): 45-day returns [29] 90. Weight (2023 154cm measured): 2,880 grams (6lbs 6oz) per SnowboardingProfiles hands-on weighing [16] 91. Weight per cm: 18.70 grams/cm — slightly heavier than 18.59 g/cm average across ~200 boards [16] 92. Weight feel on snow: Felt really light despite scales showing slightly above average [16] 93. Build quality (forum user review): Rated 10/10 — "Bataleon always seems to have a really high build quality. No flaws anywhere" [30] 94. Durability concern (Bataleon reviews page): Some reports of softer Bataleon boards breaking/cosmetically wearing; one user reported Evil Twin topsheet splitting after 15-20 days [31] 95. SnowboardingProfiles overall score: 89.7/100 [16] 96. Ranked 3rd out of 28 men's freestyle snowboards tested [16] 97. Jibbing rating: 5/5 (20/20 weighted) [16] 98. Jumps rating: 4/5 (16/20 weighted) [16] 99. Spins rating: 4.5/5 (13.5/15 weighted) [16] 100. Switch rating: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [16] 101. Butters rating: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [16] 102. Turning rating: 5/5 (5/5 weighted) [16] 103. Uneven terrain rating: 3.5/5 [16] 104. Powder rating: 2.5/5 [16] 105. Speed rating: 2/5 [16] 106. Carving rating: 2/5 [16] 107. Whitelines 100 inclusion: Disaster selected for Whitelines 100 Best Snowboard Gear Awards in 2021/22 season [32] 108. Whitelines review verdict: "solidly built, with a flex pattern and 3D profile that are perfect for park progression" [32] 109. The Inertia review: Disaster+ named "Best Jib Board" in 2026 test [33] 110. Edge catch prevention: "About as uncatchy as it gets" — 3BT virtually eliminates edge catches [16] 111. Turn initiation: Extremely easy — "just have to think about turning and it does" [16] 112. Pressability: Ultra easy to initiate a press — "barely have to lean into nose or tail" [16] 113. Pop accessibility: Easy pop with minimal effort — good for sidehits [16] 114. Beginner suitability: "Beginner suitable for sure, because of how easy it is to turn and how uncatchy it feels" [16] 115. Skate-like feel: "Contemporary nose and tail kicks deliver a skate-like feel" [34] 116. Fun factor (manufacturer site user review): "So fun, playful and pressable!" [20] 117. User review (Bataleon site): "Super fun board, very flexy flexy, forgiving and an attention-getter" [35] 118. Tree riding: Fun in trees due to quick edge-to-edge transitions [16] 119. Carving limitation: "This board doesn't carve that well… wants to skid/let go at speed" [16] 120. Speed stability limitation: Not suited for bombing hills — gets wobbly at high speed [16] 121. Powder limitation: Only average powder float due to centered twin shape and minimal sidebase uplift [16] 122. Big jumps limitation: "Super fun for smaller jumps but too soft for bigger jumps" [16] 123. Crud handling: "Gets bucked around super easy and you feel everything" [16] 124. Edge hold on ice: "Seems to wash out on ice and gets chattery at higher speeds" (forum) [30] 125. Weight concern (older model forum): "For a 153, this thing is pretty heavy" — though weight improved in more recent years [30] 126. User complaint — too soft for some: "A bit too soft for me.. no pop!" (Bataleon site review) [35] 127. Whitelines reviewer tip: "It can get flappy at speed so I'd think about sizing up" [36] 128. Nose/tail kicks: Contemporary skate-inspired kicks [34] 129. Tip/tail profile: Blunted tips — super wide [30] 130. Nose/tail shape: Identical (true twin) — same topsheet artwork in either direction [37] 131. Stance setback: Centered [16] 132. Setback inserts: Neutral stance with +2 backseat inserts for deep powder option [38] 133. 3BT description: Tip-to-tail positive camber combined with lifted sidebase contact points — minimizes edge-catch without sacrificing ollie power [20] 134. 3BT Jib tune: Widest centerbase in the Bataleon range, least sidebase uplift — optimized for presses, stable slides, powerful ollies [18] 135. SideKick description: Tips become hull-like, boosting float in deep snow and slicing through crud, also helps roll edge to edge quickly [20] 136. Flex Walls vs previous "Shock Walls": Current model uses urethane poured Flex Walls; older models (2023 and prior) used "Shock Walls" urethane infused sidewall technology [39] 137. Bi-Ax laminate description: Traditional two-way weave that is light, strong and playful; snappy without adding torsional stiffness [20] 138. Competitor: Bataleon Evil Twin — stiffer (flex 5/10), more all-mountain versatile, medium camber vs Disaster's low camber [40] 139. Competitor: Bataleon Disaster+ — upgraded version with carbon stringers, C.S.T. Super Tubes, Aramid X-Ply, Light Core, flex 3-4/10 instead of 2/10 [13] 140. Competitor: Ride Twinpig — park-focused twin, volume-shifted short/wide shape, asym sidecut, $569 USD [41] 141. Competitor: CAPiTA Defenders of Awesome (DOA) — all-mountain freestyle twin, hybrid camber, ~$580 USD, stiffer and more versatile than the Disaster [33] 142. Competitor: YES Jackpot, Lib Tech Box Knife, Never Summer Funslinger — all freestyle twins compared in same category [42] 143. Competitor within Bataleon range: Bataleon Fun.Kink — directional twin, flex 4/10, more all-mountain oriented vs park-only Disaster [43] 144. Competitor within Bataleon range: Bataleon Blow — entry-level park twin, softer flex, cheaper, sintruded base rather than sintered [44] 145. Key differentiation from competitors: Bataleon's 3BT base shape is unique and patented — no other brand offers the same 3D base construction [45] 146. Brand reputation (Whitelines): "Not many brands have had such an impact on the snowboard industry as Bataleon" [46] 147. Brand reputation (Nidecker Group position): Nidecker Group is "considered the second biggest snowboard company in the world" [3] 148. 3BT learning curve: Some riders report 3BT requires adjustment period — "it takes some time to get used to" [40] 149. 3BT polarizing opinions: "edge hold was lacking" per some forum users; others say "freakin' awesome for butters and presses" [47] 150. Brand innovation recognition: "For more than 20 years, we have led the industry in 3D snowboard tech" [48] 151. Flex rating (Bataleon own site 2025/2026 Disaster): Rated flex 2 (Soft) [49] 152. Flex rating (merchant listing for 2027): 3/10 [2] — DISAGREEMENT: Multiple retailer sources list the base Disaster as flex 2/10; the 3/10 rating may correspond to the Disaster+ or a changed spec for 2027. 153. Flex rating (Exodus Ride Shop 2025 Disaster): Flex 2 (Soft) [18] 154. Flex rating (Deckadence Skateboards listing): Soft (2/10) [38] 155. Sidecut type: Tri-radial (three-radius) [2] 156. Binding compatibility: Standard 2x4 insert pattern — compatible with virtually all major binding brands [2] 157. Flex direction: Symmetrical (true twin flex) [32] 158. Stance position: Centered [2] 159. Profile description: Low camber runs nose to tail; lower camber boards are smoother at low speeds and in powder [17] 160. Design philosophy: Stripped-back simplicity — "made a name for itself through its simplicity" keeping price down [37] 161. Value proposition: Below average price ($499 USD) vs average freestyle board price of $518 [16]
